To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the morphology, absorption spectra and fluorescence spectra of melanosomes in the RPE change with age.
(1) the absorption spectra of melanosomes increase with increasing age; (2) melanosome fluorescence increases with increasing age; and (3) lipofuscin fluorescence increases with increasing donor age.
the RPE of the human eye is a site for melanin biosynthesis throughout life and that the RPE pigment granules undergo age-related changes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the morphological, spectral and biochemical characteristics of the human RPE.
the morphological and spectral changes of melanin-containing granules within the human RHE as a function of aging
the study of the morphology, absorption spectra and fluorescence of melano- and lipofuscinosomes from human retinal pigment cells (RPE).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
melanin granules in human RPE are not inert but are metabolically active.
the RPE undergoes changes with age, but that these changes do not appear to be related to age in a simple linear fashion.
melanin granules in human RPE are present throughout life.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the RPE is a dynamic structure that changes with age.
the RPE is an active, dynamic tissue that undergoes significant morphological, chemical and spectral changes during aging.
the RPE is an active, dynamic tissue that is constantly involved in pigment metabolism and that the pigment granules of this tissue undergo age-related changes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the melanosome and liposfuscin granules within the human RPIE undergo age-related changes.
the RPE of older eyes has an increased amount of pigment and lipofuscion.
melanin is present within RPE cells throughout life, and that melanogenesis occurs within these cells, even at an advanced age.
